correctness.rationale: Each resolution update replaces every participant row by the union of participant views and leaves other rows fixed; these maps preserve componentwise unions. Therefore the suffix acts on an arbitrary input view tuple by taking the union over the contributor indices computed from singleton initial views. Applying this once to the prefix tuple and once after the occurrence \(B\) gives exactly \(F_a\) versus either \(F_a\) or \(F_a\cup U_B\), proving the criterion. If views differ, a coordinate-equality Kripke model makes distinct contributor index sets induce distinct intersection relations, proving model-independent necessity. For an empty suffix, the condition reduces to equality of participant views. Greedy deletion of immediately redundant events preserves the entire current view tuple, and every retained event strictly raises \(\sum_a |V_a|\) from \(n\) toward at most \(n^2\), giving the compression bound. The inspected verifier exhausts all groups with up to four agents for short prefixes/suffixes as a consistency check.

final_claim: For an occurrence \(B\) in an asynchronous-resolution history \(\vec P.B.\vec S\), deletion preserves every final current accessibility relation in every underlying model exactly when, for each final agent, either its suffix contributor set misses \(B\) or the prefix union contributed by \(B\) is already contained in its deletion-side final contributor union; immediate redundancy is equivalent to equality of all participant views, and every history has a current-relation-equivalent subhistory of length at most \(n(n-1)\).
